entry.title: Unleashing the Power of Absence and Surprise

link.title: Unleashing the Power of Absence and Surprise

entry.content:
Can a machine be surprised? In our work on Learning via Surprisability (LvS), we teach AI systems to form expectations and adjust when reality diverges — much as humans do. By learning from surprise, models become more efficient, adaptable, and explainable. We have applied the approach across domains including social media, political discourse, and historical text.

This post accompanies my short talk, Teaching AI the Power of Surprise. See the Learning via Surprisability research thread for the underlying methods and papers.
entry.summary: Teaching AI to learn not just from data, but from the unexpected.

entry.title: Reflections from my NetSciX’25 Keynote
entry.content: I was proud to give a keynote at NetSciX’25 in Indore, India — the flagship winter conference of the Network Science Society. I presented our interaction-driven model for analyzing the dynamics of viral transmission in real-world interactions, and the broader program of temporal-network modeling the SCAN Lab has been building. See the Temporal Networks thread for details.
entry.summary: A keynote at the flagship winter conference of the Network Science Society.

entry.title: Beyond R0: COVID-19 Transmission through Temporal Network Analysis

link.title: Beyond R0: COVID-19 Transmission through Temporal Network Analysis

entry.content: In 2019, in the middle of an Israel Science Foundation–funded effort to quantify the effects of external events on interaction networks, the COVID-19 pandemic arrived. We adapted our temporal interaction-driven contagion model to assess individual transmission risk, evaluate social-distancing policies, and analyze competition among viral strains. This line of work appeared in Scientific Reports and the Journal of Biomedical Informatics; see the Temporal Networks thread and the publications page.
entry.summary: An interaction-driven temporal model for individual risk and latent transmission.
